tweets.text:
Stacks recently released its Q3 report with updates.

Here's a short TL;DR + some of my thoughts ↓

→ Bitcoin Staking

The first two staking rounds brought in 735 BTC, with 21Shares, HashKey Cloud, and UTXO Management among the participants.

→ Liquid Staking

@StackingDao accounted for 483 BTC of the 505 BTC in the second round. It now has 636 BTC worth of stBTC in circulation.

→ STX Staking

The amount of STX staked has grown by over 25% since the PoX-5 upgrade, from 392M to 493M STX.

→ Lending

@ZestProtocol now has over $122M in deposits and $42M in loans, with around 800 BTC used as collateral.

→ Trading

Trading across Stacks DEXs reached $16.7M in a single week in September, the highest in a year, with @Bitflow leading the activity.

My guess is that BTC staking will end up benefiting more than just the staking protocols.

More people borrowing against their staked BTC → more activity in lending markets and DEXs → more fees going to different parts of the ecosystem.

Quite the opportunity for the entire ecosystem.

Disclosure: I'm a long-time $STX holder and Stacks supporter.

#Uranium #Silver #Copper #Gold
DAILY METALS PULSE | 16 October 2026
WEEKLY WRAP-UP
A bruising inflation week for precious metals. Meanwhile, the race to secure energy and raw materials keeps moving.

☢️ URANIUM
The U.S. is backing three nuclear plant restarts with up to $4.4 billion in federal loans, aiming to restore 2.25 GW. Big Tech is signing long-term power contracts. My takeaway: restarting reactors adds another source of fuel demand alongside new builds and life extensions.

🥈 SILVER
Around $57/oz late Friday, heading for a weekly loss after sharp swings. This week showed how quickly rate expectations can overwhelm the longer-term thesis. I remain bullish, but expect volatility to keep testing conviction.

🔶 COPPER
Trading around $6.50/lb, still roughly 32% above a year ago. This week also highlighted a crucial distinction: copper stockpiled in the U.S. does not automatically solve supply needs elsewhere. Watch inventory location alongside headline totals.

🥇 GOLD
Around $4,165/oz late Friday, down approximately 0.7% for the week. Hotter inflation revived rate-hike concerns, leaving gold caught between inflation protection and the pressure from higher interest rates.

My view heading into the weekend: stay selective. Prioritize projects that can turn resources into production—and companies with the funding to get there.

The next leg needs execution. ⚒️

Chamath Explains the AI Boom’s Achilles Heel

“Doesn't matter what you do, doesn't matter what you claim to do, you're going to get run over. You're going to be roadkill.

If the bond market walks the 10-year up to 5.5 and 6%, which has nothing to do with AI, it has everything to do with debt to GDP and a bunch of other factors in broad-based Western economies, any business model that thrives on a financing spread gets cornholed.

Any and every, all of them. It will not matter when the 10-year’s at 6%. It won't matter.

As long as we can keep that from happening, we're going to be fine.

So what's the most important way, I guess, post these midterms to keep the party going?

You have to really start to focus on deficits, and you have to find a fair trade where the bond market backs off.

And I think you can see it in the tape, meaning if we start proposing huge spending programs, they're going to walk the 10-year up.

That then has a negative cascade to everything.

If, however, the posture becomes much more about keeping everything calm and like, ‘Let's just tone things down and let's find the waste in the system and squeeze it all out,’ I think people will respond very favorably.

The last thing I will say is these are like Achilles' heels, meaning all of the asset value that's getting built up, but just like the great warriors, you just slice the Achilles tendon and they just crumble to the knees.

I just want to point out, this is that thing. There is no other thing.

Meaning, all this other stuff is complete goodness, but the fact that you need to finance these things in a variable rate model as a spread to the risk-free rate is the big problem in these businesses.

And you need to essentially have Microsoft, Google, Meta, and Nvidia backstop all of this in a worst case scenario because that's the only way you can withstand a one or two-year correction in this market.”

Demographics, debt, debasement. Three words that drive everything.

It starts with an aging population. Fewer workers means slower growth, so governments borrow to keep the economy moving. The debt keeps growing because the demographics leave them no other option.

That debt was never going to be paid back. So it gets managed instead... by debasing the currency. More money created every year, each unit worth a little less than the last. Slowly enough that most people never notice.

That is The Everything Code. Debasement sets the real hurdle rate for your money, and over the long run only two assets have cleared it... crypto and technology. 

But thats only the first part of the story. The Exponential Age is where everything goes vertical at once. And the end state is The Economic Singularity, where everything changes.

I've never had all of it written down in one place before. Now it's in one book, out November 3rd.

Thank you to everyone who has already pre-ordered. If youre going to read it, Id be honoured if youd consider pre-ordering... it helps the rankings, and the rankings are what get the book in front of people who have never heard any of this.

@KevinWSHPod thanks for having me on mate, pleasure as always

tweets.text:
I went from working with one agent in a chat to sitting in tmux monitoring 6 agents in parallel in my terminal.

And honestly that's about the limit of my brain. I'm constantly switching between them, remembering what each one is doing, checking who's stuck and who needs me. It's exhausting!

I can’t do that with 100 agents. Or 200. Definitely not a swarm of 200k.

The more I work this way, the more obvious it becomes that it's the wrong form factor. Even with a nice UI, I'm not going to click through every agent to figure out what's going on.

What I need is a feed. A command center that tells me what happened, what's stuck, what needs a decision from me and what I should look at next. So let the agents coordinate the work. Bring me in when I can actually help.

I want to run more agents without spending the rest of my life watching them.

The more I work this way, the more obvious it becomes that it's the wrong form factor. Even with a nice UI, I'm not going to click through every agent to figure out what's going on.

What I need is a feed. A command center that tells me what happened, what's stuck, what needs a decision from me and what I should look at next. So let the agents coordinate the work. Bring me in when I can actually help.

I want to run more agents without spending the rest of my life watching them.
